text: Esters of meta- aminobenzoic acid Proxymetacaine Esters of para- aminobenzoic acid Benzocaine Butacaine Butoxycaine Butyl aminobenzoate Chloroprocaine Oxybuprocaine Parethoxycaine Procaine Propoxycaine Tetracaine Tricaine Local Anaesthetics 1851 The symbol † denotes a preparation no longer actively marketed The symbol  denotes a substance whose use may be restricted in certain sports (see p.vii) Methaemoglobinaemia has occurred after the topical application of a eutectic preparation of prilocaine and lidocaine.8,10 Although increases in methaemoglobin concentrations are generally small after the use of this mixture in infants12,13 and children,14 some infants may be particularly susceptible to induced methaemoglo- binaemia during the first 3 months of life probably due to their limited enzyme capacity.12 The BNF states that eutectic prilo- caine/lidocaine cream may be used under specialist supervision in infants over 1 month of age, and in some other countries the cream is also licensed for limited use in neonates (see also Sur- face Anaesthesia under Lidocaine, p.1866). However, UK li- censed product information does not recommend its use in chil- dren under 1 year old. Use with drugs such as sulfonamides8 or antimalarials11 may pre- dispose to methaemoglobinaemia.
